refDefault.note: Reported as whole urea molecule (LOINC 3091-6), not urea nitrogen. Tietz adult interval 2.14-7.14 mmol/L = 12.9-42.8 mg/dL. For cross-check: Mayo BUN adult male 8-24 mg/dL x 2.14 (urea/BUN mass ratio 60/28) = ~17-51 mg/dL urea. Patient lab-printed range 10-50 mg/dL is consistent.

references.organization: Medscape (Tietz Clinical Guide to Laboratory Tests)
references.document: Lab Values, Normal Adult: Laboratory Reference Ranges in Healthy Adults — Urea
references.quote: Adults 18-60 y serum urea reference range 2.14-7.14 mmol/L (12.9-42.8 mg/dL); 60-90 y 2.86-8.21 mmol/L (17.1-49.3 mg/dL).

references.document: BUN - Overview: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN), Serum (unit code 81793)
references.quote: Males >=18 years: 8-24 mg/dL; Females >=18 years: 6-21 mg/dL (urea nitrogen; multiply by 2.14 to express as urea).

why: End product of protein/amino-acid catabolism cleared by the kidneys; elevated urea reflects reduced GFR, dehydration, high protein load or catabolism (BUN:creatinine ratio distinguishes pre-renal from renal causes).

refDefault.note: Sex-specific; male upper limit higher than female due to greater muscle mass. Mayo males >=15 y 0.74-1.35 mg/dL. Patient lab-printed upper (1.40) marginally wider.

references.document: RFAMA - Overview: Renal Function Panel, Serum (Creatinine component, unit code 113634)
references.quote: Creatinine, Males >=15 years: 0.74-1.35 mg/dL (sex-specific reference values).

why: Muscle-derived waste filtered by the glomerulus and minimally reabsorbed; the primary endogenous marker of GFR and the basis of eGFR estimation.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 1175 (Uric Acid), molecular weight 168.11 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/1175

refDefault.note: Sex-specific (male range higher). Mayo male reference 3.7-8.0 mg/dL (female 2.7-6.1); hyperuricemia defined as >8.0 mg/dL in males. Lower bound has some inter-lab variability; patient lab-printed 3.0-7.0 is narrower/lower on the top.

references.document: URIC - Overview: Uric Acid, Serum (unit code 8440)
references.quote: Hyperuricemia is most commonly defined by serum/plasma uric acid concentrations above 8.0 mg/dL in males or above 6.1 mg/dL in females; male reference interval 3.7-8.0 mg/dL, female 2.7-6.1 mg/dL.

why: Terminal product of purine metabolism; supersaturation drives gout and urate nephrolithiasis, and it is a marker in tumor lysis and metabolic syndrome.

refDefault.note: Electrolyte reported as molar concentration (SCnc). Mayo >=1 y 135-145 mmol/L. Patient lab-printed upper (148) is slightly wider.

references.document: BMAMA - Overview: Basic Metabolic Panel, Serum (Sodium component, unit code 113630)

why: Principal extracellular cation governing plasma osmolality and water distribution; dysnatremia reflects water balance and ADH/renal handling rather than total-body sodium.

refDefault.note: Molar concentration (SCnc). Mayo >=1 y 3.6-5.2 mmol/L. Hemolysis and delayed separation falsely raise results. Patient lab-printed 3.50-5.30 essentially equivalent.

references.document: BMAMA - Overview: Basic Metabolic Panel, Serum (Potassium component, unit code 113630)

why: Dominant intracellular cation; small serum shifts critically affect cardiac and neuromuscular excitability, and levels reflect renal excretion, acid-base status and aldosterone.

refDefault.note: Molar concentration (SCnc). Mayo adults >=18 y 98-107 mmol/L. Patient lab-printed 98-106 essentially equivalent.

references.document: BMAMA - Overview: Basic Metabolic Panel, Serum (Chloride component, unit code 113630)

why: Major extracellular anion tracking sodium and bicarbonate; used with the anion gap to classify metabolic acidoses and assess acid-base balance.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 5462224 (Magnesium, element), standard atomic weight 24.305 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5462224

refDefault.note: Reported as elemental mass (mg/dL); 1 mg/dL Mg = 0.4114 mmol/L. Commonly cited adult interval 1.7-2.3 mg/dL, but there is no international consensus and labs range from ~1.6-2.6 mg/dL. Patient lab-printed 1.80-2.60. Serum reflects <1% of total-body magnesium.

references.document: Magnesium: Reference Range, Interpretation, Collection and Panels
references.quote: Adult serum magnesium reference range approximately 1.7-2.3 mg/dL (0.70-0.95 mmol/L); values vary by laboratory.

references.document: Recommendation on an updated standardization of serum magnesium reference ranges
references.quote: There is currently no international consensus on the serum magnesium reference interval; standardization is recommended.

why: Cofactor for hundreds of enzymes and ATP-dependent reactions; hypomagnesemia commonly accompanies and perpetuates refractory hypokalemia and hypocalcemia.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 5462309 (Phosphorus, element), standard atomic weight 30.974 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5462309 (assays report inorganic phosphate but result expressed as elemental phosphorus mass; 1 mg/dL P = 0.3229 mmol/L)

refDefault.note: Measured as inorganic phosphate, reported as elemental phosphorus mass (mg/dL). Mayo adult 2.5-4.5 mg/dL, matching patient lab-printed range.

references.quote: Adults: 2.5-4.5 mg/dL for serum inorganic phosphorus.

why: Essential for ATP, nucleic acids and bone mineral; serum levels are tightly co-regulated with calcium by PTH, vitamin D and FGF23, and disturbances are central to CKD-mineral bone disorder.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 5460341 (Calcium, element), standard atomic weight 40.078 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5460341

refDefault.note: Total calcium as elemental mass (mg/dL); 1 mg/dL Ca = 0.2495 mmol/L. Widely used adult reference 8.6-10.2 mg/dL; interpret with albumin (correct +0.8 mg/dL per 1 g/dL albumin below 4.0) or measure ionized calcium. Patient lab-printed 8.40-10.20 slightly wider on the low end.

references.document: Serum Calcium: Reference Range, Interpretation, Collection and Panels
references.quote: Adult total serum calcium reference range approximately 8.6-10.2 mg/dL (2.15-2.55 mmol/L).

references.document: CA - Overview: Calcium, Total, Serum (unit code 601514)
references.quote: Total serum calcium adult reference values (age-banded, approximately 8.6-10.0 mg/dL for adults).

why: Total serum calcium (protein-bound + ionized) reflects skeletal and mineral homeostasis under PTH and vitamin D; abnormalities point to parathyroid disease, malignancy, vitamin D disorders and CKD.

refDefault.note: Intact (2nd/3rd-generation) PTH immunoassay reference interval 15-65 pg/mL (ECLIA); assay- and vitamin-D-dependent. Must be interpreted together with serum calcium. Matches patient lab-printed range.

references.document: Parathyroid Hormone (PTH), Intact, Serum (PTHI) test catalog
references.quote: Reference range for intact parathyroid hormone 15-65 pg/mL by electrochemiluminescent immunoassay (ECLIA).

references.organization: Mayo Clinic Laboratories Network Reference Lab
references.document: Parathyroid Hormone (PTH), Intact, Plasma or Serum (PTH-INT)
references.quote: Intact PTH reference values 15-65 pg/mL; values >65 pg/mL with hypercalcemia suggest primary hyperparathyroidism.

why: Principal regulator of calcium and phosphate; the master test for distinguishing PTH-dependent (primary/secondary hyperparathyroidism) from PTH-independent causes of calcium disorders and for CKD-MBD monitoring.
